title: Base: MG996R at its real height (blocks 5 mm shorter)
how: The MG996R is 42.9 mm overall (case 38.1 + spline), not 47.9: in the old CAD its spline was 5 mm too high, so on the real servo it stops short of the horn under the turret plate. The 2 blocks its tabs screw into are now 5 mm shorter, so the servo sits 5 mm higher and the spline reaches the horn.

title: Wrist servo 3.5 mm further out
how: The real MG90S body is 32.7 mm long (the CAD had 28.5): its end reached the base's bearing tower whenever the carriage was low. The wrist servo now sits 3.5 mm further out: the arm beam is 3.5 mm longer, the gripper frame 3.5 mm shorter. Fingers, gears and the can position are unchanged.

title: Carriage: printed on its side, gussets, pockets
how: The old carriage snapped where the arm meets the wrist bracket (printed standing, the layers ran across the arm). Now: printed on its side (layers along the arm), 2 side gussets at that corner, 5 walls + 30 % infill, LM6UU pockets with a pointed top (no support inside) and ~12.25 mm as printed, and the link's pivot block notched so the upper bearing goes in.

title: Lift: the bagged horn's last hole + a new link
how: No horn in the servo bag reaches 20 mm, so the crank now uses the single-arm horn's last hole (14 mm). A new, longer link (11.2 mm between holes) and a bigger swing (−34° … +34°, firmware LIFT_UP 98) keep the lift at 15.7 mm (≥ 15.2 required); the crank top stays 0.7 mm under the top cap.

title: Gripper frame: bigger horn opening, wings cut off
how: Horn opening Ø16 (was 14) so a screwdriver reaches the horn screws; the plate wings that nothing touches are cut off (−27 % plastic). Old right finger and the new left finger both fit.

title: Horns from the servo bags
how: Lift: single-arm horn, link on its last hole. Wrist: cross horn, long arms cut to 11 mm, 4 screws through its arm holes into 4 pilots in the frame flange. Gripper: double-arm horn, arms cut to 7 mm, hub up on the left gear, 2 screws; the SG90's spline goes down into its hub. Where a hole doesn't line up, drill 1/16″ through the horn.

title: Spine: room for the screw heads
how: The #6 pan heads (Ø6.6) hit the spine wall 2 mm from the holes: a half-round notch beside each hole.
